headline: Mortgage rates are under upward pressure. The 10-year Treasury is 5.15% (+6 bp on the day) and the modeled 30-year sits near 7.45%.
summary: The 10-year Treasury is at 5.15%, +6 bp on the day. Mortgage rates take their direction from the 10-year first. Between the last two published mortgage surveys the 30-year moved +0 bp. That breaks down exactly: -12 bp from Treasuries and +12 bp from the mortgage spread. The mortgage/10-year spread is 230 bp, which is normal and sits at the 64th percentile of the last 10 years. The long-run average is 208 bp, so roughly 22 bp of the current mortgage rate is spread rather than Treasury yield. Intraday spread movement is not observable here. Without a live MBS feed the daily read assumes the spread held and moves the rate with the 10-year only.
